  4. project-management/sessions/ledger.yaml
  5. On-disk run records: dark-factory runs/, sprint-factory runs/, session autopilot runs.log,
     harness-scorecard.yaml, repo-local .claude/sprint-harness-state.yaml, .claude/ralph-loop.local.md

Signal classes per item (transcripts):
  base_*        what usage_scan.py already counts (Skill name, Agent subagent_type, str slash prompt)
  slash_list    slash command inside a list-form user prompt (scanner skips list content)
  slash_queued  slash command typed while busy (queued_command attachment; scanner skips attachments)
  slash_args    item named inside the args of another slash command (e.g. /ralph-loop:ralph-loop "sprint-crawl X")
  skill_args    item named inside a Skill tool `args` string
  prompt_lead   human prompt that STARTS with the item name (e.g. "sprint-crawl KTP-1")
  prompt_any    human prompt that mentions the item anywhere (upper bound; includes discussion)
  dispatch_strong  Agent call of another type whose prompt points at the item definition file
                   or says "you are <item>" / "follow <item>"
  dispatch_any  Agent call of another type whose prompt mentions the item (upper bound)
  def_load      Read/Bash/Grep/Glob touching the item definition file (load, or maintenance)
  workflow_run  Workflow tool call whose script path or name names the item
  attrib        rows attributed to the item (attributionSkill / attributionAgent)
  headless      any of the strong signals inside an entrypoint=sdk-cli (claude -p / SDK) file
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import datetime as dt
import json
import re
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

H = Path.home()
PROJECTS = H / ".claude/projects"
PM = H / "Developer/grp-beklever-com/project-management"
SHARED = H / ".claude-shared-config"
OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
START = dt.datetime(2026, 9, 1, tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc)
END = dt.datetime(2026, 11, 13, tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc)

ITEMS = {
    "night-crawl": r"night[- ]crawl",
    "dev-crawl": r"dev[- ]crawl",
    "sprint-crawl": r"sprint[- ]crawl|sprint-harness:sprint-crawl",
    "dark-factory": r"dark[- ]factory",
    "sprint-factory": r"sprint[- ]factory",
    "supervisr-autopilot": r"supervisr[- ]autopilot",
    "autonomous-ticket-ship": r"autonomous[- ]ticket[- ]ship",
    "session:autopilot": r"session:autopilot|autopilot-run\.js",
    "ralph-loop": r"ralph[- ]loop(?!-preflight)|setup-ralph-loop|ralph-loop\.local\.md",
    "ralph-loop-preflight": r"ralph-loop-preflight",
    "crawl-adversarial-review-cascade": r"crawl-adversarial-review-cascade",
}
RX = {k: re.compile(r"(?<![\w-])(?:" + v + r")(?![\w])", re.I) for k, v in ITEMS.items()}
LEAD = {k: re.compile(r"^\s*(?:" + v + r")\b", re.I) for k, v in ITEMS.items()}
DEF_FILES = {
    "night-crawl": r"agents/night-crawl\.md", "dev-crawl": r"agents/dev-crawl\.md",
    "sprint-crawl": r"agents/sprint-crawl\.md|commands/sprint-crawl\.md|sprint-harness/",
    "dark-factory": r"skills/dark-factory/", "sprint-factory": r"skills/sprint-factory/",
    "supervisr-autopilot": r"agents/supervisr-autopilot\.md", "autonomous-ticket-ship": r"skills/autonomous-ticket-ship/",
    "session:autopilot": r"skills/autopilot/SKILL\.md|sessions/autopilot/", "ralph-loop": r"ralph-loop/\d|ralph-loop/(?:commands|scripts|hooks)",
    "ralph-loop-preflight": r"skills/ralph-loop-preflight/", "crawl-adversarial-review-cascade": r"skills/crawl-adversarial-review-cascade/",
}
DEF_RX = {k: re.compile(v) for k, v in DEF_FILES.items()}
STRONG_DISPATCH = {k: re.compile(r"(?:agents|skills)/" + re.escape(k.split(":")[-1]) + r"(?:\.md|/SKILL\.md)|you are (?:the )?(?:" + ITEMS[k] + r")|(?:follow|run|act as|execute) (?:the )?(?:" + ITEMS[k] + r")", re.I) for k in ITEMS}
OVERNIGHT = re.compile(r"overnight|over night|while i(?:'m| am)? (?:sleep|away|out)|go autonomous|work autonomously|autonomous(?:ly)? (?:run|mode|work)|one-?shot this|surprise me|until morning|tonight|by (?:the )?morning|all night", re.I)
ANALYSIS = re.compile(r"usage_scan|measuring-otter|prune (?:the |my )?harness|harness prun|invocation-detection", re.I)
CMD_NAME = re.compile(r"<command-name>/?([\w:.-]+)</command-name>")
CMD_ARGS = re.compile(r"<command-args>(.*?)</command-args>", re.S)
SLASH = re.compile(r"^\s*/([\w:.-]+)(.*)", re.S)
SYSTEM_PROMPT_PREFIX = ("<task-notification", "<local-command", "Caveat:", "This session is being continued", "<system-reminder", "[Request interrupted")


def ts_of(raw):
    try:
        t = dt.datetime.fromisoformat(str(raw).replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        return t if t.tzinfo else t.replace(tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc)
    except ValueError:
        return None


def in_window(t):
    return t is not None and START <= t < END


def norm_cmd(name):
    name = name.lstrip("/")
    for k in ITEMS:
        short = k.split(":")[-1]
        if name == k or name.endswith(":" + short) or name == short:
            if k == "session:autopilot" and name == "autopilot":
                return k
            if k == "session:autopilot" and not name.endswith("autopilot"):
                continue
            return k
    return None


def text_of_content(c):
    if isinstance(c, str):
        return c
    if isinstance(c, list):
        return "\n".join(b.get("text", "") for b in c if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get("type") == "text")
    return ""


class Tally:
    def __init__(self):
        self.rows = defaultdict(Counter)        # item -> signal -> count
        self.sess = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(set))  # item -> signal -> sessions
        self.last = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(str))

    def add(self, item, sig, session, day):
        self.rows[item][sig] += 1
        self.sess[item][sig].add(session)
        self.last[item][sig] = max(self.last[item][sig], day)


STRONG = ("base_skill", "base_agent", "base_slash", "slash_list", "slash_queued", "slash_args", "skill_args",
          "prompt_lead", "dispatch_strong", "workflow_run")


def handle_prompt(T, text, session, day, form, side, analysis_sessions, overnight, headless):
    if not text or text.lstrip().startswith(SYSTEM_PROMPT_PREFIX):
        return
    cmd = None
    m = CMD_NAME.search(text) if "<command-name>" in text else None
    args = ""
    if m:
        cmd = m.group(1)
        a = CMD_ARGS.search(text)
        args = a.group(1) if a else ""
    else:
        s = SLASH.match(text)
        if s:
            cmd, args = s.group(1), s.group(2)
    if cmd:
        item = norm_cmd(cmd)
        if item:
            T.add(item, {"str": "base_slash", "list": "slash_list", "queued": "slash_queued"}[form], session, day)
        for k, rx in RX.items():
            if k != item and rx.search(args or ""):
                T.add(k, "slash_args", session, day)
        return
    if side:
        return  # sidechain "prompts" are written by a parent agent, counted as dispatch
    if ANALYSIS.search(text):
        analysis_sessions.add(session)
    for k in ITEMS:
        if LEAD[k].search(text):
            T.add(k, "prompt_lead", session, day)
        if RX[k].search(text):
            T.add(k, "prompt_any", session, day)
    if OVERNIGHT.search(text):
        overnight.append((session, day, form, text.strip().replace("\n", " ")[:160], headless))


def scan_transcripts():
    T = Tally()
    analysis_sessions, overnight = set(), []
    session_items = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(Counter))  # session -> item -> strong signal count
    session_activity = defaultdict(Counter)  # session -> Skill/Agent/Workflow names
    headless_sessions, scheduled_sessions, bg_sessions = set(), set(), set()
    files = Counter()
    for f in PROJECTS.rglob("*.jsonl"):
        if f.stat().st_mtime < START.timestamp():
            continue
        kind = "workflow-agent" if "/workflows/" in str(f) else "subagent" if "/subagents/" in str(f) else "main"
        files[kind] += 1
        headless = False
        for line in f.open(errors="replace"):
            try:
                r = json.loads(line)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                continue
            t = ts_of(r.get("timestamp")) if r.get("timestamp") else None
            if r.get("entrypoint") == "sdk-cli":
                headless = True
            if not in_window(t):
                continue
            day = t.date().isoformat()
            session = r.get("sessionId") or f.stem
            if headless:
                headless_sessions.add(session)
            if r.get("turnOrigin") == "scheduled":
                scheduled_sessions.add(session)
            if r.get("sessionKind") == "bg":
                bg_sessions.add(session)
            side = bool(r.get("isSidechain")) or kind != "main"
            for key in ("attributionSkill", "attributionAgent"):
                v = r.get(key)
                if isinstance(v, str):
                    it = norm_cmd(v)
                    if it:
                        T.add(it, "attrib", session, day)
            typ = r.get("type")
            msg = r.get("message") or {}
            content = msg.get("content")
            if typ == "user" and not r.get("isMeta") and not r.get("isCompactSummary"):
                if isinstance(content, str):
                    handle_prompt(T, content, session, day, "str", side, analysis_sessions, overnight, headless)
                elif isinstance(content, list) and any(isinstance(b, dict) and b.get("type") == "text" for b in content):
                    handle_prompt(T, text_of_content(content), session, day, "list", side, analysis_sessions, overnight, headless)
            if typ == "attachment":
                a = r.get("attachment") or {}
                if a.get("type") == "queued_command" and not a.get("isMeta"):
                    handle_prompt(T, text_of_content(a.get("prompt")), session, day, "queued", side, analysis_sessions, overnight, headless)
            if typ == "assistant" and isinstance(content, list):
                for b in content:
                    if not isinstance(b, dict) or b.get("type") != "tool_use":
                        continue
                    name, inp = b.get("name", ""), b.get("input") or {}
                    if name == "Skill":
                        sk = str(inp.get("skill", ""))
                        session_activity[session]["skill:" + sk] += 1
                        it = norm_cmd(sk)
                        if it:
                            T.add(it, "base_skill", session, day)
                        for k, rx in RX.items():
                            if k != it and rx.search(str(inp.get("args", ""))):
                                T.add(k, "skill_args", session, day)
                    elif name in ("Agent", "Task"):
                        st = inp.get("subagent_type") or "general-purpose"
                        session_activity[session]["agent:" + st] += 1
                        it = norm_cmd(st)
                        if it:
                            T.add(it, "base_agent", session, day)
                        p = str(inp.get("prompt", "")) + " " + str(inp.get("description", "")) + " " + str(inp.get("name", ""))
                        for k, rx in RX.items():
                            if k == it:
                                continue
                            if STRONG_DISPATCH[k].search(p):
                                T.add(k, "dispatch_strong", session, day)
                            if rx.search(p):
                                T.add(k, "dispatch_any", session, day)
                    elif name == "Workflow":
                        sp = json.dumps({k: inp.get(k) for k in ("scriptPath", "name", "script_path", "workflow") if k in inp})
                        session_activity[session]["workflow:" + (Path(str(inp.get("scriptPath", "?"))).name)] += 1
                        for k, rx in RX.items():
                            if rx.search(sp) or (k == "dark-factory" and "dark-factory" in sp) or (k == "session:autopilot" and "autopilot-run" in sp):
                                T.add(k, "workflow_run", session, day)
                    elif name in ("Read", "Bash", "Grep", "Glob", "Edit", "Write"):
                        s = " ".join(str(inp.get(k, "")) for k in ("file_path", "command", "path", "pattern"))
                        for k, rx in DEF_RX.items():
                            if rx.search(s):
                                T.add(k, "def_load", session, day)
                        if "setup-ralph-loop" in s or "ralph-loop.local.md" in s:
                            T.add("ralph-loop", "ralph_mechanics", session, day)
                        if "sprint-harness-state.yaml" in s:
                            T.add("sprint-crawl", "harness_state_touch", session, day)
    # per-session strong signals
    for item, sigs in T.sess.items():
        for sig, ss in sigs.items():
            if sig in STRONG:
                for s in ss:
                    session_items[s][item][sig] += 1
    for item in list(T.rows):
        hs = set()
        for sig in STRONG:
            hs |= T.sess[item][sig] & headless_sessions
        if hs:
            T.rows[item]["headless_sessions"] = len(hs)
    return T, analysis_sessions, overnight, session_items, session_activity, headless_sessions, scheduled_sessions, bg_sessions, files


def scan_history():
    """~/.claude/history.jsonl: one row per typed prompt. Fields: display, timestamp(ms), project."""
    c = defaultdict(Counter)
    overnight = 0
    total = 0
    p = H / ".claude/history.jsonl"
    for line in p.open(errors="replace"):
        try:
            r = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        ms = r.get("timestamp")
        if not isinstance(ms, (int, float)):
            continue
        t = dt.datetime.fromtimestamp(ms / 1000, dt.timezone.utc)
        if not in_window(t):
            continue
        total += 1
        d = str(r.get("display", ""))
        if ANALYSIS.search(d):
            c["_analysis"]["prompts"] += 1
            continue
        s = SLASH.match(d)
        if s:
            it = norm_cmd(s.group(1))
            if it:
                c[it]["slash"] += 1
            for k, rx in RX.items():
                if k != it and rx.search(s.group(2)):
                    c[k]["slash_args"] += 1
        else:
            for k in ITEMS:
                if LEAD[k].search(d):
                    c[k]["lead"] += 1
                if RX[k].search(d):
                    c[k]["any"] += 1
        if OVERNIGHT.search(d):
            overnight += 1
    return c, overnight, total


def scan_codex():
    c = defaultdict(Counter)
    files = 0
    root = H / ".codex/sessions"
    for f in root.rglob("*.jsonl"):
        if f.stat().st_mtime < START.timestamp():
            continue
        files += 1
        sess = f.stem
        for line in f.open(errors="replace"):
            try:
                r = json.loads(line)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                continue
            if not in_window(ts_of(r.get("timestamp", ""))):
                continue
            pl = r.get("payload") or {}
            if pl.get("type") == "message" and pl.get("role") == "user":
                txt = " ".join(b.get("text", "") for b in pl.get("content", []) if isinstance(b, dict))
                if txt.lstrip().startswith(("<environment_context", "<user_instructions", "# AGENTS.md", "<permissions")):
                    continue
                for k in ITEMS:
                    if LEAD[k].search(txt) or re.match(r"^\s*[/$]" + re.escape(k.split(":")[-1]), txt):
                        c[k]["prompt_lead"] += 1
                    if RX[k].search(txt):
                        c[k]["prompt_any"] += 1
            elif pl.get("type") in ("function_call", "custom_tool_call", "local_shell_call"):
                a = str(pl.get("arguments") or pl.get("input") or pl.get("action") or "")
                for k, rx in DEF_RX.items():
                    if rx.search(a):
                        c[k]["def_load"] += 1
    return c, files


def scan_ledger():
    c = defaultdict(Counter)
    p = PM / "sessions/ledger.yaml"
    try:
        import yaml
        data = yaml.safe_load(p.read_text())
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        return {"_error": Counter({str(e)[:80]: 1})}
    recs = []

    def walk(x):
        if isinstance(x, dict):
            if any(k in x for k in ("created", "started", "date", "modified")) and any(k in x for k in ("file", "slug", "theme", "intent", "ticket", "name")):
                recs.append(x)
            else:
                for v in x.values():
                    walk(v)
        elif isinstance(x, list):
            for v in x:
                walk(v)
    walk(data)
    for r in recs:
        raw = str(r.get("created") or r.get("started") or r.get("date") or r.get("modified") or "")[:10]
        inwin = "2026-09-01" <= raw <= "2026-11-12"
        blob = json.dumps(r, default=str)
        for k, rx in RX.items():
            if rx.search(blob):
                c[k]["in_window" if inwin else "other_dates"] += 1
        if "autopilot" in r:
            c["session:autopilot"][f"autopilot_field_{r.get('autopilot')}"] += 1
    c["_records"]["total"] = len(recs)
    return c


def scan_run_records():
    out = {}
    df = sorted((SHARED / "skills/dark-factory/runs").glob("run-*.y*ml"))
    out["dark-factory runs/ (window)"] = sum(1 for f in df if "2026-09-01" <= f.name[4:14] <= "2026-11-12")
    out["dark-factory runs/ (all)"] = len(df)
    tickets = {re.sub(r"-(run\d+|slice\d+|phase\d+|issue\d+)$", "", f.stem[15:]) for f in df if "2026-09-01" <= f.name[4:14] <= "2026-11-12"}
    out["dark-factory distinct tickets (window)"] = len(tickets)
    sf = [f for f in (SHARED / "skills/sprint-factory/runs").rglob("*") if f.is_file()]
    out["sprint-factory runs/ files (all)"] = len(sf)
    out["sprint-factory runs/ files mtime in window"] = sum(1 for f in sf if START.timestamp() <= f.stat().st_mtime < END.timestamp())
    log = PM / "sessions/autopilot/runs.log"
    out["session autopilot runs.log lines in window"] = sum(1 for l in log.read_text().splitlines() if "2026-09-01" <= l[:10] <= "2026-11-12") if log.exists() else "absent"
    sc = H / ".claude/harness-scorecard.yaml"
    out["harness-scorecard.yaml entries"] = sc.read_text().count("ticket") if sc.exists() else "absent"
    found = Counter()
    for root in (H / "Developer/grp-beklever-com", H / "Developer/supervisr-ai", H / "Developer/gabriel-amyot"):
        if not root.exists():
            continue
        for depth_glob in ("*/.claude/*", "*/*/.claude/*", "*/*/*/.claude/*"):
            for f in root.glob(depth_glob):
                if f.name in ("sprint-harness-state.yaml", "ralph-loop.local.md") or f.name.startswith("audit"):
                    win = START.timestamp() <= f.stat().st_mtime < END.timestamp()
                    found[f"{f.name} ({'mtime in window' if win else 'older'})"] += 1
    out["repo-local state files"] = dict(found) or "none found (depth <= 3 under org roots)"
    return out


def main():
    T, analysis, overnight, session_items, activity, headless, scheduled, bg, files = scan_transcripts()
    hist, hist_overnight, hist_total = scan_history()
    codex, codex_files = scan_codex()
    ledger = scan_ledger()
    records = scan_run_records()
    sigs = ["base_skill", "base_agent", "base_slash", "slash_list", "slash_queued", "slash_args", "skill_args", "prompt_lead",
            "prompt_any", "dispatch_strong", "dispatch_any", "def_load", "workflow_run", "attrib", "ralph_mechanics", "harness_state_touch", "headless_sessions"]
    lines = ["# Autonomy gap audit (transcripts 2026-09-01..2026-11-12)", "",
             f"Files scanned: {dict(files)}. Headless (sdk-cli) sessions: {len(headless)}. Scheduled-turn sessions: {len(scheduled)}. Background (bg) sessions: {len(bg)}.",
             f"Analysis sessions excluded from nothing but flagged: {len(analysis)}.", "",
             "## Rows per signal (sessions in brackets)", "",
             "| item | " + " | ".join(sigs) + " |", "|---|" + "---|" * len(sigs)]
    for k in ITEMS:
        cells = []
        for s in sigs:
            n = T.rows[k][s]
            ns = len(T.sess[k][s]) if s != "headless_sessions" else ""
            cells.append(f"{n} ({ns})" if n and ns != "" else str(n))
        lines.append(f"| {k} | " + " | ".join(cells) + " |")
    lines += ["", "## Strong-signal sessions per item, excluding analysis sessions", ""]
    for k in ITEMS:
        ss = {s for s, it in session_items.items() if k in it} - analysis
        ss_all = {s for s, it in session_items.items() if k in it}
        last = max((T.last[k][s] for s in STRONG if T.last[k][s]), default="never")
        lines.append(f"- {k}: {len(ss)} sessions (incl. analysis: {len(ss_all)}), last strong signal {last}")
    lines += ["", "## ~/.claude/history.jsonl (typed prompts)", "", f"Prompts in window: {hist_total}. Overnight-intent prompts: {hist_overnight}.", ""]
    for k in ITEMS:
        lines.append(f"- {k}: {dict(hist.get(k, {})) or 0}")
    lines.append(f"- analysis prompts skipped: {dict(hist.get('_analysis', {}))}")
    lines += ["", f"## Codex (~/.codex/sessions, {codex_files} files with mtime in window)", ""]
    for k in ITEMS:
        lines.append(f"- {k}: {dict(codex.get(k, {})) or 0}")
    lines += ["", "## Ledger (sessions/ledger.yaml)", ""] + [f"- {k}: {dict(v)}" for k, v in ledger.items()]
    lines += ["", "## On-disk run records", ""] + [f"- {k}: {v}" for k, v in records.items()]
    # overnight intent: what ran
    ran = Counter()
    rows = []
    for s, day, form, snippet, hl in overnight:
        items = sorted(set(session_items.get(s, {})))
        acts = activity.get(s, Counter())
        top = ", ".join(n for n, _ in acts.most_common(6))
        ran[" + ".join(items) or "(no autonomy item)"] += 1
        rows.append(f"{day} [{form}{' headless' if hl else ''}] {'ANALYSIS ' if s in analysis else ''}session={s[:8]} items={items or '-'} top={top or '-'} :: {snippet}")
    lines += ["", f"## Overnight-intent prompts in transcripts: {len(overnight)} (sessions {len({o[0] for o in overnight})})", "",
              "What autonomy item ran in the same session (strong signals):", ""] + [f"- {k}: {v}" for k, v in ran.most_common()]
    (OUT / "overnight_prompts.txt").write_text("\n".join(rows) + "\n")
    (OUT / "gap-audit-report.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    print("\n".join(lines))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

H = Path.home(); P = H / ".claude/projects"
S = dt.datetime(2026, 9, 1, tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc); E = dt.datetime(2026, 11, 13, tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc)

        if r.get("entrypoint") == "sdk-cli": headless = True

        sid = r.get("sessionId") or f.stem
        if r.get("cwd") and sid not in sess_cwd: sess_cwd[sid] = r["cwd"].replace(str(H), "~")

        if r.get("turnOrigin") == "scheduled": sched.add(sid)
        c = (r.get("message") or {}).get("content")
        if r.get("type") == "assistant" and isinstance(c, list):
            for b in c:
                if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get("type") == "tool_use":
                    n = b.get("name", ""); inp = b.get("input") or {}
                    if "orkflow" in n or n in ("RemoteTrigger", "CronCreate", "ScheduleWakeup"): tools[n] += 1
                    label = None
                    if n == "Skill": label = "skill:" + str(inp.get("skill"))
                    elif n in ("Agent", "Task"): label = "agent:" + str(inp.get("subagent_type") or "general-purpose")

                        sp = Path(str(inp.get("scriptPath") or inp.get("name") or "?")).name
                        label = "workflow:" + sp; wf_days[ts[:10]] += 1; wf_scripts[sp] += 1
                    if label: rows_by_session[sid].append(label)
for s in hl_sessions:
    hl_cwd[re.sub(r"/[^/]*-worktrees?/.*|/\.claude/worktrees/.*", "/<worktree>", sess_cwd.get(s, "?"))[:70]] += 1
    for a in set(rows_by_session.get(s, [])): hl_act[a] += 1
for s in sched:

print("workflow scripts", wf_scripts.most_common(12))

    for k in re.findall(r"^([a-z_]+):", t, re.M): fields[k] += 1

print("df run days", Counter(days))
print("df run top-level fields", [k for k, _ in fields.most_common(30)])
print("df run selected values", hosts.most_common(30))

```text
Your persona: direct, analytical, confrontational toward vague language — but a coach, not a dictator. You think out loud from two angles: "If I'm the developer, what do I build?" and "If I'm QA, what do I assert?" When a spec is bad, you explain precisely what will go wrong during implementation, not just that it's vague.

## Persona file

Before running, read your full persona from:
`~/.claude-shared-config/bmad/custom/spec-coach.md`

## Invocation

```
leo-ac-scan [--project KEY] [--reporter USER] [--assignee USER] [--status STATUS] [--jql "JQL"]
```

**Defaults (when no args given):**
- reporter = gabriel
- status excludes: Done, Closed, Won't Do
- all projects in the org

**Parameter override examples:**
- `leo-ac-scan --project SPV` — only SPV project
- `leo-ac-scan --assignee gabriel` — only tickets assigned to gabriel
- `leo-ac-scan --reporter daniel.craggs` — only Daniel's tickets (comment-only mode)
- `leo-ac-scan --jql "sprint in openSprints() AND project = SPV"` — raw JQL override (overrides all other params)

## Phase 4 — Present to User

After writing the report to disk:

1. Show the summary table (key, rating, top finding per ticket)
2. Show REWRITE tickets in full — proposed rewrites + comment drafts
3. Show NEEDS WORK tickets — proposed rewrites + comment drafts
4. Skip SHIP IT detail (just list the keys)

Then ask: "Which tickets do you want me to act on?" and wait.

Do NOT post any comment or update any ticket until the user explicitly confirms.

## Phase 5 — Execute Approved Actions

For each approved ticket:

**If reporter = gabriel (Gab's ticket):**
```bash
cd ~/.claude/skills/jira && python3 jira_skill.py update {KEY} --description "{rewritten description}" --skip-disclaimer
```

**If reporter = other (teammate's ticket):**
Post a coaching comment as Leo. Follow this format:
```
[automated] claude-code | {model} | session: {date} | agent: Leo, Spec Coach
---
Hey {reporter first name} — Leo here. I trace tickets from a dev and QA lens before implementation starts. {specific finding per AC, actor perspective}

If the intent is clear to the team, no action needed. Flagging early so the questions surface before implementation rather than during.

Leo
```

Rules for the comment:
- Direct, concrete, never generic
- One paragraph per AC with a finding — no more
- Frame from dev OR QA perspective, not both (pick the one that's more revealing for that AC)
- End with the coaching close: invite dialogue, don't demand action
- No emojis (Jira rule)
- Show the comment to the user before posting

After all actions, report: "Posted {N} comments, updated {N} descriptions."

## What This Agent Does NOT Do

- Modify ACs on tickets not reported by gabriel (comment only)
- Post anything without user confirmation
- Invent behavior that isn't in the AC — only flag what's missing
- Run silently — always show the scan report before acting
```

## zoom-out

description: >
  Quick plain-language recap of the work just done and where things stand.
  Use when you've lost the thread after a run of diffs and tool calls, or
  you've stepped away and come back unsure what was going on.
disable-model-invocation: true

## improve-codebase-architecture
description: Find deepening opportunities in a codebase, informed by the domain language in CONTEXT.md and the decisions in docs/adr/. Use when the user wants to improve architecture, find refactoring opportunities, consolidate tightly-coupled modules, or make a codebase more testable and AI-navigable.
---

# Improve Codebase Architecture

Surface architectural friction and propose **deepening opportunities** — refactors that turn shallow modules into deep ones. The aim is testability and AI-navigability.
## grilling
description: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
---

Interview the user relentlessly until you reach a shared understanding. Map this as a **design tree**: every decision branches into the decisions that hang off it.

Work the tree in **rounds**. The **frontier** is every decision whose prerequisites are already settled: the questions you can ask _now_ without guessing at answers you haven't heard yet. Ask the whole frontier in one round: number each question and give your recommended answer. Then wait for the user's answers before the next round.
## grill-me
description: Interview the user relentlessly about a plan or design until reaching shared understanding, resolving each branch of the decision tree. Use when user wants to stress-test a plan, get grilled on their design, or mentions "grill me".
---

Interview me relentlessly about every aspect of this plan until we reach a shared understanding. Walk down each branch of the design tree, resolving dependencies between decisions one-by-one. For each question, provide your recommended answer.

Ask the questions one at a time.
## grill-with-docs
description: Grilling session that challenges your plan against the existing domain model, sharpens terminology, and updates documentation (CONTEXT.md, ADRs) inline as decisions crystallise. Use when user wants to stress-test a plan against their project's language and documented decisions.
---

<what-to-do>

Interview me relentlessly about every aspect of this plan until we reach a shared understanding. Walk down each branch of the design tree, resolving dependencies between decisions one-by-one. For each question, provide your recommended answer.
## spillover-scan
description: "Aggregate accepted adversarial findings, warnings, and test gaps from closed tickets into a tracking ticket. Classifies by severity, recommends priority order, and posts to Jira."
user_invocable: true
## klever-test
description: "Klever testing hub for suite and evidence testing: Playwright regression, backend API e2e, AC validation, proximity 14-UC suite, UX dogfood, and the sprint proof runner. Use when the user says 'run the e2e/regression suite', 'run the backend tests', 'generate proof', 'sprint proof', 'AC evidence', 'prove the sprint', or wants Jira-ready test artifacts for a ticket or sprint. For LIVE
user_invocable: true

## Output format

Lead with a one-line verdict (approve / approve-with-follow-ups / blocked), then list findings, highest impact first. Order by impact, not by where they appear in the diff:

1. Structural regressions this change introduces
2. Missed judo moves with a visible path to a dramatically simpler implementation
3. Spaghetti and branching complexity the change adds
4. Boundary, abstraction, or contract problems that obscure the design
5. File-size and decomposition concerns
6. Remaining legibility and maintainability notes

Write each finding in this shape so the gate stays visible:

```
[blocks merge | follow-up] <file>:<area> — <the problem in one line>
  Simpler shape: <the concept this would delete, and the move that deletes it>
```

A short list of high-conviction findings beats a long list of cosmetic notes. Flooding the review with nits while a structural problem sits unaddressed is a failure of the review, not a sign of thoroughness.

## Tone

Be direct, serious, and demanding about quality while staying respectful of the author. When a change makes the codebase messier, say so plainly. When it missed a chance at a dramatic simplification, say that too. Soft-pedaling a real maintainability problem into a mild suggestion does the author no favors.

Calibration, the register to aim for:

- `this pushes the file well past a comfortable size. can we decompose it first?`
- `this adds another special-case branch into an already busy flow. can we move it behind its own abstraction?`
- `this works, but it makes the surrounding code more spaghetti. let's keep the behavior and restructure the implementation.`
- `this feels like feature logic leaking into a shared path. can we isolate it?`
- `this abstraction doesn't seem to be earning its keep. can we keep the direct flow instead?`
- `why does this need a cast / optional here? can we make the boundary explicit?`
- `this looks like a bespoke version of something we already have. can we reuse the canonical helper?`
- `i think there's a code-judo move here that makes this much simpler. can we reframe so these branches disappear?`
- `this moves complexity around but doesn't delete it. is there a way to make the model itself simpler?`

## Approval bar

Correct behavior is the floor, not the bar. Block merge while this change leaves any of these unaddressed:

- a structural regression the change introduces
- a visible judo move, squarely within this change's scope, that would delete real complexity
- an unjustified file-size explosion
- spaghetti growth from new special-case branching
- a hacky or magical abstraction that makes the code harder to reason about
- wrapper, cast, or optionality churn that obscures the real design
- an architecture-boundary leak or a needless duplicate of a canonical helper

Treat each as a presumptive blocker the author should fix or justify. For larger structural debt the change merely sits near rather than creates, record a clear follow-up and approve.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""ledger_probe.py: group sessions/ledger.yaml into list entries (no PyYAML) and count
entries mentioning each autonomy item, by entry date (created/started/date) in or out of window.
For overnight-tagged entries in the window, print slug/theme only (no bodies)."""
import re
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from pathlib import Path
L = Path.home() / "Developer/grp-beklever-com/project-management/sessions/ledger.yaml"
pats = {"sprint-crawl": r"sprint[- ]crawl", "dark-factory": r"dark[- ]factory", "sprint-factory": r"sprint[- ]factory",
        "autopilot-field": r"^\s*autopilot:", "overnight": r"overnight|night run|night-run|autonomous"}
entries, cur = [], []
for line in L.read_text().splitlines():
    if re.match(r"^\s{0,4}- ", line) and cur:
        entries.append(cur); cur = []
    cur.append(line)
entries.append(cur)
c = defaultdict(Counter); hits = defaultdict(list)
for e in entries:
    blob = "\n".join(e)
    m = re.search(r"(?:created|started|date|initiated):\s*['\"]?(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})", blob)
    d = m.group(1) if m else "?"
    win = "2026-09-01" <= d <= "2026-11-12"
    name = re.search(r"(?:slug|file|name|theme):\s*(.+)", blob)
    for k, p in pats.items():
        if re.search(p, blob, re.I | re.M):
            c[k]["window" if win else ("undated" if d == "?" else "outside")] += 1
            if win and k in ("overnight", "sprint-crawl", "sprint-factory", "autopilot-field"):
                hits[k].append(f"{d} {name.group(1)[:90] if name else '?'}")
print("entries", len(entries))
for k, v in c.items(): print(k, dict(v))
for k, v in hits.items():
    print("==", k); print("\n".join(sorted(v)[:25]))
EOF
python3 ledger_probe.py
```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Third pass: weekly counts of jira_skill.py results vs Atlassian/Notion MCP calls.
Run: python3 mcp_usage_scan3.py > mcp_usage_scan3.out.txt"""
import glob, json, os, datetime
from collections import Counter

ROOT = os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/projects")
mod, ok, mcp = Counter(), Counter(), Counter()


def wk(ts):
    d = datetime.date.fromisoformat(ts[:10])
    return (d - datetime.timedelta(days=d.weekday())).isoformat()


for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT, "**", "*.jsonl"), recursive=True):
    pend = set()
    with open(f, errors="replace") as fh:
        for line in fh:
            if "jira_skill" not in line and "mcp__claude_ai_" not in line and not pend:
                continue
            try:
                r = json.loads(line)
            except Exception:
                continue
            ts = r.get("timestamp") or ""
            if not ("2026-09-01" <= ts[:10] < "2026-11-13"):
                continue
            c = (r.get("message") or {}).get("content")
            if not isinstance(c, list):
                continue
            for b in c:
                if not isinstance(b, dict):
                    continue
                if b.get("type") == "tool_use":
                    n = b.get("name", "")
                    if n == "Bash" and "jira_skill.py" in str((b.get("input") or {}).get("command", "")):
                        pend.add(b.get("id"))
                    for k in ("Atlassian", "Notion"):
                        if n.startswith("mcp__claude_ai_" + k):
                            mcp[(wk(ts), k)] += 1
                elif b.get("type") == "tool_result" and b.get("tool_use_id") in pend:
                    pend.discard(b.get("tool_use_id"))
                    if "No module named" in str(b.get("content")):
                        mod[wk(ts)] += 1
                    else:
                        ok[wk(ts)] += 1

weeks = sorted(set(mod) | set(ok) | {w for w, _ in mcp})
print("week_of     jira_ok  jira_nomodule  atlassian_mcp  notion_mcp")
for w in weeks:
    print(f"{w}  {ok[w]:7d}  {mod[w]:13d}  {mcp[(w, 'Atlassian')]:13d}  {mcp[(w, 'Notion')]:10d}")

```

# claude.ai connector use in the terminal (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-12)

Scope: Klever. Source: `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl` (1,432 files, main threads and subagent files).
Method: three scripts in this folder read the transcripts. Only their output was read.

- `mcp_usage_scan.py` gives counts, the trigger class, and samples. Output: `mcp_usage_scan.out.txt`.
- `mcp_usage_scan2.py` gives jira_skill.py error kinds, the stated reason before each call, and the MCP lines in subagent prompts. Output: `mcp_usage_scan2.out.txt`.
- `mcp_usage_scan3.py` gives the weekly trend. Output: `mcp_usage_scan3.out.txt`.

Total: 204 calls. Atlassian 111, Notion 61, Google Drive 18, Gmail 12, Slack 2. All 204 calls ran in Klever sessions. 203 of them ran from `project-management`. One ran from `klever-ai-workshop`.

## 1. Counts per connector

| Connector | Calls | Sessions | Main / subagent | Sep / Oct / Nov | Tools |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Atlassian | 111 | 25 | 64 / 47 | 5 / 31 / 75 | getJiraIssue 59, searchJiraIssuesUsingJql 49, search 2, getTransitionsForJiraIssue 1 |
| Notion | 61 | 8 | 17 / 44 | 1 / 40 / 20 | notion-fetch 38, notion-search 13, notion-get-version-changes 5, notion-get-comments 4, notion-query-data-sources 1 |
| Google Drive | 18 | 3 | 4 / 14 | 0 / 13 / 5 | search_files 9, read_file_content 4, get_file_metadata 3, get_file_permissions 2 |
| Gmail | 12 | 2 | 6 / 6 | 0 / 12 / 0 | search_threads 8, get_thread 4 |
| Slack | 2 | 2 | 1 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 2 | authenticate 2 (no data was read) |

All calls were reads. No call created, edited, or transitioned anything. getTransitionsForJiraIssue only reads the list of transitions.

## 2. Trigger classification

The script used heuristics. The class "agent prompt named the MCP" means that the subagent prompt text names the connector. The orchestrator model wrote that prompt itself. No skill template supplied it.

| Trigger | Atlassian | Notion | Drive | Gmail | Slack |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| User explicitly asked for MCP / connector | 10 | 4 | 7 | 6 | 1 |
| Orchestrator wrote "use the Atlassian MCP / Notion connector" in a subagent prompt | 23 | 39 | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| User or agent asked for the data, and the model picked the MCP | 60 | 11 | 4 | 2 | 0 |
| Model picked the MCP with no related keyword in the prompt | 18 | 7 | 4 | 4 | 1 |
| A skill or agent definition told the model to use the connector | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The most frequent subagent-prompt lines that the orchestrator wrote:

- `...claude.ai Notion connector: load it with ToolSearch query "select:mcp__claude_ai_Notion__notion-fetch,..."` (19 calls)
- `...claude.ai Notion connector tools (load via ToolSearch "select:mcp__claude_ai_Notion__notion-fetch,...")` (18 calls)
- `Jira (read-only): use the Atlassian MCP tools if available (ToolSearch ...) or python3 ~/.claude/skills/jira/jira_skill.py` (5 calls)
- `Find the ticket(s): search Jira (Atlassian MCP tools via ToolSearch "searchJiraIssuesUsingJql", or the jira skill ...)` (5 calls)

In these prompts, the MCP is offered as the first option, and jira_skill.py comes second.

Before each Atlassian call, the model stated a reason in 54 of 111 cases. The reasons: the MCP was named (36), the full body or comments were needed (13), a search was needed (10), and jira_skill.py failed (7). In 57 cases, the model gave no reason.

## 3. Root causes

### Atlassian

1. **jira_skill.py could not import `jira` until 2026-11-06.** In the window, the scripts found 371 jira_skill.py calls and 62 errors. 39 of the errors were `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'jira'`. No system Python on this Mac has the `jira` package. The SKILL.md examples still say `python3 jira_skill.py`. Commit `79b5f08` (2026-11-06) added a `uv run --script` shebang and a re-run under uv. After that date, the no-module errors drop to 0.
2. **The failure taught a habit that the fix did not remove.** The weekly counts:

   | Week of | jira_skill OK | jira_skill no-module | Atlassian MCP | Notion MCP |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | 2026-10-26 | 102 | 20 | 31 | 21 |
   | 2026-11-02 | 89 | 11 | 38 | 1 |
   | 2026-11-09 | 96 | 0 | 37 | 19 |

   Atlassian use did not fall after the fix. In the last session state before each call, jira_skill.py had failed for 17 calls and had worked for 33 calls. For 61 calls, the transcript had no jira_skill.py call before the MCP call. So the failure explains part of the use, not most of it.
3. **The orchestrator offers the MCP to subagents.** It writes "Atlassian MCP via ToolSearch ... or jira_skill.py" in research prompts. The MCP comes first. Subagents take the first option.
4. **The bibliothèque endorses the MCP.** `documentation/bibliotheque/stack/jira-sprint-wiring-atlassian-mcp.md` answers "How do I assign a ticket to a sprint via Atlassian MCP?". ALIASES.md carries `atlassian-mcp-origin` and `jira-sprint-wiring`. When a model reads the library, it learns that the MCP is a normal path.
5. **Read-back after a write.** jira-skill-gotchas says that `--description-file` can report success while the description stays empty. The model reads the ticket back through getJiraIssue, because the MCP is a separate, trusted channel.
6. **The tools are always loaded.** The claude.ai connectors appear as deferred tools in every session. One ToolSearch call loads them. No setting denies them.

### Notion

1. **The local mirror cannot fetch on this Mac.** `notion-checkout/.mcp.json` does not exist. `fetch-shard.sh` stops with "isolated fetch config missing". `skills/notion/recovery.md` (2026-11-11) records this. The new mirror has 1 page. That page "was staged by hand from a claude.ai connector fetch". The old 232-page mirror is not recovered. So for any page that is not in the mirror, the connector is the only path that works.
2. **The orchestrator tells subagents to use the connector.** 39 of the 61 calls came from subagents. Their prompts said "claude.ai Notion connector: load it with ToolSearch ...". Two sessions (6797c86a and fc2cb8d0) account for most of these calls.
3. **Some tasks need live data that the mirror does not keep.** These tasks are version history (`notion-get-version-changes`), comments, and "is this page current?". The 400c3298 SOP drift check used all three. The mirror does not store version history.
4. **Old docs still point at the MCP.** `documentation/notion-wiki/INDEX.md` says "confirm freshness against the source via Notion MCP". The `klever-wiki` plugin (`wiki-refresh.md`, `wiki-search/SKILL.md`) names `mcp__notion__notion-fetch`. That is a different server name, but it frames the MCP as the refresh path.

### Google Drive and Gmail

There is no local skill for Drive or Gmail. 30 calls ran in 4 sessions. Most of them were "search everywhere" sessions (d8a8e06b: find Raj's idea after Slack failed with `not_authed`). Others needed sheet IDs or OAuth email access. These calls were not a bypass of a local tool.

### Slack

There were 2 calls, and both were `authenticate`. The connector was never authenticated, and no data was read. In both sessions the local `slack` skill was active. The model tried the connector after the skill had no token. In the current session, the claude.ai Slack connector shows as blocked by the managed policy.

### Skill and agent text

A grep of `~/.claude-shared-config` (skills, agents, plugins, hooks, CLAUDE.md) and `project-management/CLAUDE.md` found no instruction to call `mcp__claude_ai_Atlassian*` or `mcp__claude_ai_Notion*`. The only mentions:

- `skills/notion/SKILL.md` and `nx.py`: never register the Notion MCP at user scope. Use it only through the isolated `.mcp.json` fetch.
- `skills/notion/scheduled-refresh-task.md`: the Cowork refresh task uses "the Notion MCP". The file says that it is not verified if Cowork uses the claude.ai account connector.
- `plugins/klever-wiki`: names `mcp__notion__notion-fetch`. That is not the claude.ai connector.

No skill tells the model to use the connectors. The model chose them, or the orchestrator model wrote them into subagent prompts.

## 4. What breaks if all claude.ai connectors are disabled in the terminal

| Flow | Effect | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Jira read, search, comments, transitions | No break. jira_skill.py covers get, search, comments, description, history, and transitions. It works since 2026-11-06. | Change the SKILL.md examples to `uv run`. Remove "Atlassian MCP" from the orchestrator prompt habits. |
| Sprint assignment as described in `jira-sprint-wiring-atlassian-mcp.md` | The doc becomes wrong. `jira_skill.py update --sprint` exists. | Update the bibliothèque page and the aliases to the jira_skill path. |
| Confluence or Rovo `search` | Lost. jira_skill has no Confluence command. In the window it was used 2 times only. | Accept the loss, or add a Confluence command later. |
| Notion page fetch for a page that is not in the mirror | **Breaks today.** `.mcp.json` is missing, so the isolated fetch cannot run. The mirror has 1 page. | First do the `.mcp.json` trust and OAuth steps in `recovery.md`. Then recover or rebuild the mirror. Disable the connector only after that. |
| Notion version history, comments, freshness checks | Break unless the isolated fetch server exposes them. | Use the isolated session for these, or allow the connector for each session when necessary. |
| Cowork scheduled Notion refresh | Unknown. The task file says that it is not verified if Cowork uses the claude.ai connector. | Use the order in the task file: prove that the task runs without the connector, then disable it. Note: `disableClaudeAiConnectors` in the terminal settings may not affect Cowork at all. Verify this. |
| Google Drive and Gmail lookups | Lost. No local skill exists. Use was rare (4 sessions). | Accept the loss, or keep these two connectors enabled with `deniedMcpServers` for the others. |
| Slack | No break. The connector was never authenticated, and the local `slack` skill is the path. | None. |

Recommended order: (1) fix the Notion isolated fetch, (2) correct the bibliothèque Atlassian MCP page and the SKILL.md `python3` examples, (3) deny Atlassian and Notion in the terminal with `deniedMcpServers`, and keep Drive and Gmail if needed, (4) consider `disableClaudeAiConnectors` later. Also correct `library/context/mcp-server-scoping-and-isolation.md`. It says that settings cannot disable claude.ai connectors, and that is outdated.

## Open Questions / Unverified

- The trigger classes come from keyword heuristics. They are not a manual reading of every call.
- "jira_skill failed in session" uses a loose error regex. The 62-error count uses a stricter regex. The no-module count of 39 is exact.
- It is not verified whether Cowork uses the claude.ai Notion connector.
- It is not verified whether the isolated Notion server exposes version history and comments.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""followup_probe.py: aggregate follow-ups for autonomy_gap_audit.py (counts only).

1. history.jsonl date range (does the typed-prompt log cover the window?)
2. Workflow / scheduling tool names, Workflow script names and run days
3. Headless (entrypoint=sdk-cli) sessions: cwd and what they ran
4. Scheduled-turn sessions: what they ran
5. dark-factory run records in the window: days and launch fields
6. Ledger entries (sessions/ledger.yaml, parsed without PyYAML) mentioning autonomy items
Usage: python3 followup_probe.py
"""
import datetime as dt
import json
import re
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

H = Path.home()
P = H / ".claude/projects"
S = dt.datetime(2026, 9, 1, tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc)


def in_win(day):
    return "2026-09-01" <= day <= "2026-11-12"


def history():
    months, first, last = Counter(), None, None
    for line in (H / ".claude/history.jsonl").open(errors="replace"):
        try:
            r = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        ms = r.get("timestamp")
        if isinstance(ms, (int, float)):
            t = dt.datetime.fromtimestamp(ms / 1000, dt.timezone.utc)
            months[t.strftime("%Y-%m")] += 1
            first, last = min(first or t, t), max(last or t, t)
    print("history.jsonl range", first, last, sorted(months.items())[-5:])


def transcripts():
    tools, wf_days, wf_scripts = Counter(), Counter(), Counter()
    hl, sched, cwd, acts = set(), set(), {}, defaultdict(set)
    for f in P.rglob("*.jsonl"):
        if f.stat().st_mtime < S.timestamp():
            continue
        headless = False
        for line in f.open(errors="replace"):
            try:
                r = json.loads(line)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                continue
            if r.get("entrypoint") == "sdk-cli":
                headless = True
            ts = str(r.get("timestamp") or "")
            if not in_win(ts[:10]):
                continue
            sid = r.get("sessionId") or f.stem
            if r.get("cwd") and sid not in cwd:
                cwd[sid] = r["cwd"].replace(str(H), "~")
            if headless:
                hl.add(sid)
            if r.get("turnOrigin") == "scheduled":
                sched.add(sid)
            c = (r.get("message") or {}).get("content")
            if r.get("type") != "assistant" or not isinstance(c, list):
                continue
            for b in c:
                if not isinstance(b, dict) or b.get("type") != "tool_use":
                    continue
                n, inp = b.get("name", ""), b.get("input") or {}
                if "orkflow" in n or n in ("RemoteTrigger", "CronCreate", "ScheduleWakeup"):
                    tools[n] += 1
                if n == "Skill":
                    acts[sid].add("skill:" + str(inp.get("skill")))
                elif n in ("Agent", "Task"):
                    acts[sid].add("agent:" + str(inp.get("subagent_type") or "general-purpose"))
                elif n == "Workflow":
                    sp = Path(str(inp.get("scriptPath") or inp.get("name") or "?")).name
                    acts[sid].add("workflow:" + sp)
                    wf_days[ts[:10]] += 1
                    wf_scripts[sp] += 1
    hl_cwd, hl_act, sc_act = Counter(), Counter(), Counter()
    for s in hl:
        hl_cwd[re.sub(r"/\.claude/worktrees/.*|-worktrees?/.*", "/<worktree>", cwd.get(s, "?"))[:70]] += 1
        hl_act.update(acts.get(s, ()))
    for s in sched:
        sc_act.update(acts.get(s, ()))
    print("workflow/scheduling tool names", tools.most_common())
    print("workflow scripts", wf_scripts.most_common(12))
    print("workflow run days", sorted(wf_days.items()))
    print("headless sessions", len(hl), "cwd", hl_cwd.most_common(8))
    print("headless sessions with no Skill/Agent/Workflow call", sum(1 for s in hl if not acts.get(s)))
    print("headless top activities (sessions)", hl_act.most_common(15))
    print("scheduled sessions", len(sched), "activities", sc_act.most_common(10))


def df_runs():
    days, vals = Counter(), Counter()
    for f in sorted((H / ".claude-shared-config/skills/dark-factory/runs").glob("run-*.yaml")):
        d = f.name[4:14]
        if not in_win(d):
            continue
        t = f.read_text(errors="replace")
        days[d] += 1
        for k in ("host", "launcher", "launch", "executor", "mode", "entrypoint", "invoked_by", "terminal_state", "outcome", "status"):
            m = re.search(rf"^\s*{k}:\s*(.+)$", t, re.M)
            if m:
                vals[f"{k}={m.group(1).strip()[:28]}"] += 1
    print("df run days", sorted(days.items()))
    print("df run field values", vals.most_common(25))


def ledger():
    L = H / "Developer/grp-beklever-com/project-management/sessions/ledger.yaml"
    pats = {"sprint-crawl": r"sprint[- ]crawl", "dark-factory": r"dark[- ]factory", "sprint-factory": r"sprint[- ]factory",
            "autopilot-field": r"^\s*autopilot:", "overnight": r"overnight|night[- ]run|autonomous"}
    entries, cur = [], []
    for line in L.read_text().splitlines():
        if re.match(r"^\s{0,4}- ", line) and cur:
            entries.append(cur)
            cur = []
        cur.append(line)
    entries.append(cur)
    c, hits = defaultdict(Counter), defaultdict(list)
    for e in entries:
        blob = "\n".join(e)
        m = re.search(r"(?:created|started|date|initiated):\s*['\"]?(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})", blob)
        d = m.group(1) if m else "?"
        nm = re.search(r"(?:slug|file|name|theme):\s*(.+)", blob)
        for k, p in pats.items():
            if re.search(p, blob, re.I | re.M):
                c[k]["window" if in_win(d) else ("undated" if d == "?" else "outside")] += 1
                if in_win(d) and k != "dark-factory":
                    hits[k].append(f"{d} {nm.group(1)[:90] if nm else '?'}")
    print("ledger entries", len(entries))
    for k, v in c.items():
        print(" ", k, dict(v))
    for k, v in hits.items():
        print("  ==", k)
        for h in sorted(v)[:20]:
            print("    ", h)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    history()
    df_runs()
    ledger()
    transcripts()

```

## Real overlaps

1. **Own code diff, automated.** adversarial-cascade, crawl-adversarial-review-cascade, pr-review, thermo-nuclear, built-in code-review, simplify and security-review all review the same target. They differ by depth and by lens, but nothing tells Gabriel which one to pick.
2. **Two Codex review loops for the same diff.** adversarial-cascade Phase 2 and klever-mr external-merge-gate both send the branch diff to `codex exec` and parse a `VERDICT: PASS|BLOCK` line. service-factory Phase 4b is a third copy. Only adversarial-cascade has scripts (`build_codex_prompt.py`, `run_codex.sh`, `triage.py`).
3. **Trigger collision.** "adversarial review" starts both adversarial-cascade and crawl-adversarial-review-cascade. "check my work" (crawl) and "check my changes" (pr-review) are near duplicates. Both cascades share one H1 title.
4. **Security.** pr-review Step 5 (OWASP table) and built-in security-review do the same job.
5. **Maintainability.** thermo-nuclear and built-in simplify have the same lens. thermo-nuclear is stricter and only reports. simplify edits.
6. **AC review.** ticket-scan and story-quality-gate both start with Leo on ACs. story-quality-gate adds Winston and Amelia but needs BMAD story files that the current factories do not produce.

## Gaps

1. **pr-review cannot run its main step.** The toolkit it delegates to is disabled and not installed. Every run uses the unnamed "native reviewers" fallback.
2. **No GitHub teammate review.** colleague-review (GitHub, Supervisr) is archived. pr-review's description now says teammate review means Klever GitLab only. If Gabriel reviews a GitHub PR for someone (wayfinder issues live on GitHub), no tool covers it except built-in code-review.
3. **No single entry point for PR review.** Own PR, teammate MR and Codex merge gate live in three places (pr-review, colleague-review-klever, klever-mr reference).
4. **Responding to review comments on your own MR.** review-responder and pr-response-sweep are archived (GitHub, Supervisr). Klever GitLab has no equivalent. This may be fine. It is a gap to name, not to fill.
5. **External post path.** colleague-review-klever posts without `/post-comment`. The CLAUDE.md rule and the agent disagree.

## Consolidation proposal

### The recommended review toolset and the rule

| When | Use | Why this one |
|---|---|---|
| A human must look at a diff or plan | [crit:crit](file:///Users/gamyot/.claude/plugins/cache/crit) | Already in CLAUDE.md. Only tool with use. |
| Quick automated pass on your own diff | code-review (built-in, no local file) | No file to maintain. Effort levels. `--fix` when wanted. |
| Your own PR or MR, before you ask for review | [pr-review](file:///Users/gamyot/.claude-shared-config/skills/pr-review/SKILL.md) "mine" mode | Isolated clone, Jira AC, then built-in code-review and security-review instead of the dead toolkit. |
| A teammate's MR or PR | [pr-review](file:///Users/gamyot/.claude-shared-config/skills/pr-review/SKILL.md) "teammate" mode, which dispatches [colleague-review-klever](file:///Users/gamyot/.claude-shared-config/agents/colleague-review-klever.md) for Klever GitLab | One entry point for all PR review. The agent stays the executor. |
| A second model must attack a risky diff | [adversarial-cascade](file:///Users/gamyot/.claude-shared-config/skills/adversarial-cascade/SKILL.md) (`--skip-quinn` for Codex only) | It owns the only scripted Codex loop. |
| Tests may be lying | [test-adversarial](file:///Users/gamyot/.claude-shared-config/skills/test-adversarial/SKILL.md) | Unique. Mutation script. |
| A decision or idea needs a critic | [challenge](file:///Users/gamyot/.claude-shared-config/skills/challenge/SKILL.md) (Claude critiques) or [grilling](file:///Users/gamyot/.claude-shared-config/skills/grilling/SKILL.md) (Claude interviews you) | Different directions. Keep both. |
| ACs on a ticket | [ticket-scan](file:///Users/gamyot/.claude-shared-config/agents/ticket-scan.md) | Works on plain Jira tickets. |
| Docs tree | [tech-doc-review-flow](file:///Users/gamyot/.claude-shared-config/skills/tech-doc-review-flow/SKILL.md) | Selection record: keep. |

### Merge (edit, nothing removed)
1. **pr-review becomes the PR review hub.** Add a mode switch: "mine" (current steps, with Step 6 calling built-in `/code-review` at high effort and `/security-review`) and "teammate" (dispatch colleague-review-klever for Klever GitLab, built-in `/code-review` for GitHub). Fix `when_not`: the cascade is the heavy option, not the light one. Alternative for Gabriel: re-enable `pr-review-toolkit` instead. That keeps Step 6 as written but adds 6 plugin agents to the listing.
2. **One Codex review procedure.** klever-mr external-merge-gate and service-factory Phase 4b call adversarial-cascade's `scripts/run_codex.sh` and `triage.py` instead of their own prose copies. Their gates and stop rules stay where they are.
3. **Fix stale text in challenge.** Remove `/supervisr-review`. Say "ticket-scan agent", not `/ticket-scan`.
4. **Split triggers.** Remove "adversarial review" and "check my work" from crawl-adversarial-review-cascade (if it stays). Rename its H1.

I wrote the review cluster deep dive to `/Users/gamyot/Developer/grp-beklever-com/project-management/sessions/active/measuring-otter/deep-dives/review.md`. I changed nothing in the harness.

**The matrix in one line.** Seven tools review your own code diff. Teammate merge requests (MRs), tests, acceptance criteria (ACs) and docs each have only one or two. The only review tool with measured use is crit (5 calls in the window). Every other member has 0 calls, built-ins included. The usage scanner undercounts slash commands, so I also searched all transcripts on this machine for slash and Skill-tool use of each member. Each search returned zero.

**Facts I verified**
- `pr-review-toolkit` is set to `false` in `enabledPlugins` and is not installed. So Step 6 of pr-review never runs the toolkit. It always uses the unnamed fallback reviewers.
- `superpowers` is also disabled, but `harness-overrides.yaml` still routes code review to it.
- You do real teammate MR reviews. The Klever SOP on colleague MR reviews cites reviews on 2026-09-16 and 2026-10-14, even though no agent dispatch was recorded.
- Codex sessions are not in the data. The transcript count of real `codex exec` runs timed out three times, so that number is not measured.
- The prune lane has already staged three agents into `_archive/agents/`: colleague-review (GitHub), review-responder and pr-response-sweep.

**Overlaps**
- Seven tools on one target: adversarial-cascade, crawl cascade, pr-review, thermo-nuclear, and the built-in code-review, simplify and security-review.
- Three copies of the Codex review loop: adversarial-cascade, the klever-mr external merge gate and service-factory Phase 4b. Only adversarial-cascade has scripts.
- "adversarial review" triggers both cascades, and both files use the same title.
- The OWASP step in pr-review duplicates the built-in security-review.
- ticket-scan and story-quality-gate both start with Leo reviewing ACs.

**Proposal**
- **Make pr-review the one entry point for PR review.** Its "mine" mode calls the built-in code-review and security-review in place of the dead toolkit. Its "teammate" mode dispatches colleague-review-klever for GitLab. The other choice is to turn the toolkit back on.
- **One rule for everything else.** Use crit when a human must look. Use the built-in code-review for a quick pass and adversarial-cascade for a Codex attack. Use test-adversarial for tests, challenge or grilling for decisions, and ticket-scan for ACs.
- **Keep one Codex procedure.** The klever-mr merge gate and service-factory would call the adversarial-cascade scripts and stop keeping their own prose copies.
- **Archive candidates, your call on each:**
  - crawl-adversarial-review-cascade. Archiving it breaks one line in bmad-epic-lifecycle and one in a library file.
  - story-quality-gate. It needs BMAD story files and has not been edited since April.
  - The stale superpowers route in `harness-overrides.yaml`.

  Keep thermo-nuclear, because a slash-only skill costs nothing at load. java-quality and pre-ship-check are not reviewers, so they move to other clusters.
- **Lines that change:**
  - One routing line in the CLAUDE.md "Inline Review with Crit" section.
  - Line 16 of `skills/INDEX.md`.
  - Several `harness-overrides.yaml` lines whose "when not" text sends code review to adversarial-cascade.
  - Rows 17, 18 and 89 of `docs/harness-skill-selection.md`.
  - The pr-review description, its "when not" text (it calls the cascade "light", which is backwards) and its Step 6.
  - challenge, which points to a `/supervisr-review` that does not exist and calls ticket-scan a skill.

**Decisions for you**
- colleague-review-klever posts its comments straight to GitLab, not through `/post-comment`. That conflicts with the CLAUDE.md rule. Do you allow it as an exception, or route it through `/post-comment`?
- No tool reviews a teammate's GitHub PR now. Is the built-in `/code-review --comment` enough, or do you restore colleague-review from the archive?

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""df_run_origin_probe.py: for each day with a dark-factory run record, count
(a) Claude transcript rows that day, (b) Claude tool_use calls whose input names dark-factory,
(c) Claude Workflow calls, (d) Codex session files that day whose content names dark-factory.
Explains run records that have no matching Claude Workflow call. Counts only."""
import json
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

H = Path.home()
runs = Counter(f.name[4:14] for f in (H / ".claude-shared-config/skills/dark-factory/runs").glob("run-*.yaml")
               if "2026-09-01" <= f.name[4:14] <= "2026-11-12")
days = set(runs)
rows, df_tool, wf, sk = Counter(), Counter(), Counter(), Counter()
for f in (H / ".claude/projects").rglob("*.jsonl"):
    for line in f.open(errors="replace"):
        d = line[line.find('"timestamp":"') + 13:][:10] if '"timestamp":"' in line else ""
        if d not in days:
            continue
        rows[d] += 1
        if '"tool_use"' not in line:
            continue
        try:
            r = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        for b in (r.get("message") or {}).get("content") or []:
            if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get("type") == "tool_use":
                s = json.dumps(b.get("input"))
                if "dark-factory" in s:
                    df_tool[d] += 1
                if b.get("name") == "Workflow":
                    wf[d] += 1
                if b.get("name") == "Skill" and "dark-factory" in s:
                    sk[d] += 1
codex = Counter()
for f in (H / ".codex/sessions").rglob("*.jsonl"):
    parts = f.parts
    try:
        d = f"{parts[-4]}-{parts[-3]}-{parts[-2]}"
    except IndexError:
        continue
    if d in days and "dark-factory" in f.read_text(errors="replace"):
        codex[d] += 1
print("day | df run records | claude rows | claude tool_use naming dark-factory | Skill dark-factory | Workflow calls | codex files naming dark-factory")
for d in sorted(days):
    print(f"{d} | {runs[d]} | {rows[d]} | {df_tool[d]} | {sk[d]} | {wf[d]} | {codex[d]}")

```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""coverage_by_day.py: per-day coverage of the three local activity stores, 2026-09-01..2026-11-12.

claude_rows     rows in ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl with that day's timestamp (json-parsed)
history_prompts typed prompts in ~/.claude/history.jsonl that day
codex_files     ~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/*.jsonl files for that day
Prints a summary and the days where history has prompts but transcripts have no rows (lost transcripts).
Writes coverage_by_day.tsv next to this script."""
import datetime as dt
import json
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

H = Path.home()
OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
S, E = dt.date(2026, 9, 1), dt.date(2026, 11, 12)
days = [(S + dt.timedelta(n)).isoformat() for n in range((E - S).days + 1)]
rows, hist, codex, rows_by_project = Counter(), Counter(), Counter(), Counter()
for f in (H / ".claude/projects").rglob("*.jsonl"):
    for line in f.open(errors="replace"):
        try:
            ts = str(json.loads(line).get("timestamp") or "")[:10]
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        if S.isoformat() <= ts <= E.isoformat():
            rows[ts] += 1
hist_projects = Counter()
for line in (H / ".claude/history.jsonl").open(errors="replace"):
    try:
        r = json.loads(line)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        continue
    ms = r.get("timestamp")
    if isinstance(ms, (int, float)):
        d = dt.datetime.fromtimestamp(ms / 1000, dt.timezone.utc).date().isoformat()
        if d in rows or S.isoformat() <= d <= E.isoformat():
            hist[d] += 1
for f in (H / ".codex/sessions").rglob("*.jsonl"):
    p = f.parts
    d = f"{p[-4]}-{p[-3]}-{p[-2]}"
    if S.isoformat() <= d <= E.isoformat():
        codex[d] += 1
lost = [d for d in days if hist[d] and not rows[d]]
dark = [d for d in days if not hist[d] and not rows[d]]
(OUT / "coverage_by_day.tsv").write_text("day\tclaude_rows\thistory_prompts\tcodex_files\n" +
                                          "\n".join(f"{d}\t{rows[d]}\t{hist[d]}\t{codex[d]}" for d in days) + "\n")
print(f"days in window: {len(days)}")
print(f"days with claude transcript rows: {sum(1 for d in days if rows[d])}")
print(f"days with typed prompts (history): {sum(1 for d in days if hist[d])}")
print(f"days with codex sessions: {sum(1 for d in days if codex[d])}")
print(f"days with prompts but NO transcript rows (lost transcripts): {len(lost)}; prompts on those days: {sum(hist[d] for d in lost)}")
print("   ", ", ".join(lost))
print(f"days with neither: {len(dark)}")
first_cov = min((d for d in days if rows[d]), default=None)
print(f"first day with transcript rows: {first_cov}")
by_month = Counter()
for d in days:
    by_month[(d[:7], "rows")] += rows[d]
    by_month[(d[:7], "prompts")] += hist[d]
    by_month[(d[:7], "transcript_days")] += 1 if rows[d] else 0
print(sorted(by_month.items()))

```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""ledger_vs_local.py: how many ledger entries (sessions + handoffs) dated in the window fall on days
with NO local Claude transcript rows? Those sessions ran on another machine or host.
Needs coverage_by_day.tsv (run coverage_by_day.py first). Also counts host hints in the ledger."""
import re
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

H = Path.home()
OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
cov = {}
for line in (OUT / "coverage_by_day.tsv").read_text().splitlines()[1:]:
    d, rows, hist, codex = line.split("\t")
    cov[d] = (int(rows), int(hist), int(codex))
L = H / "Developer/grp-beklever-com/project-management/sessions/ledger.yaml"
entries, cur = [], []
for line in L.read_text().splitlines():
    if re.match(r"^\s{0,4}- ", line) and cur:
        entries.append(cur)
        cur = []
    cur.append(line)
entries.append(cur)
c, hosts = Counter(), Counter()
for e in entries:
    blob = "\n".join(e)
    m = re.search(r"(?:created|started|date):\s*['\"]?(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})", blob)
    if not m or m.group(1) not in cov:
        continue
    rows, hist, codex = cov[m.group(1)]
    c["local claude day" if rows else ("codex-only day" if codex else "no local activity day")] += 1
    for k in ("host", "machine", "hostname", "device", "runtime", "origin"):
        for v in re.findall(rf"^\s*{k}:\s*(.+)$", blob, re.M):
            hosts[f"{k}={v.strip()[:30]}"] += 1
print("ledger entries dated in window, by local coverage of that day:", dict(c))
print("host hints:", hosts.most_common(10) or "none")

```

# Overnight rounds on a map

Use this only when Gabriel explicitly asks to run a map over several nights ("run another round on
this map", "work this map overnight") and the destination is a live system. Invocation stays manual.
For one ticket overnight, use `sprint-crawl`. For a dependency-linked set of Jira tickets, use
`sprint-factory`. This file adds a **contract** around the rounds. It does not add an executor.

Execution on a map is an override of "Plan, don't do". The map's `## Notes` must say that the
map carries execution. If it does not, stop and ask.

## 1. The charter

Before round one, write a charter file (for example `HANDOFF.md` in the run folder) and link it
from the map's Notes. Every agent in every round reads it first. It holds:

- **Destination**: the live state that ends the map, stated so a test can check it.
- **Verified facts**: each with its evidence or `verified_against` stamp. No unverified claims.
- **Authority**: what agents may do without asking (for example: deploy to dev) and what needs
  Gabriel (prod, IAM, shared CI variables, data mutation, external posts). The global shipping
  safeguards apply. The charter can narrow them, never widen them.
- **Hard rules and incident rules**: what to do on a failed deploy, a data risk, or a blocked gate.

Decisions taken during a round are appended to the charter as dated sections. Do not rewrite
earlier sections.

## 2. One round

1. **Task list.** Take the map frontier, plus any explicit ask from Gabriel. Explicit asks go first.
   Order tasks only by hard dependencies.
2. **Per task:** implement, then QA with live proof, then at most a bounded fix loop, then record.
   Use the existing executors: `dark-factory` for a ticket that needs a build line, `sprint-crawl`
   for one long unattended ticket. Do not copy their gates into the round.
3. **A blocked task** gets one short unblock spike. If the spike fails, record the blocker on the
   ticket and move to the next task.
4. **Record** every task: a comment on its ticket (through `wayfinder_runs.py resolve` or `report`),
   an update to the run STATE file, and a commit of the run folder after a secret scan.

## 3. Gate rules

- A gate never passes on a rollback, a revert, or a "best effort" result. A rolled-back change is a

Date: 2026-11-13. Session: measuring-otter. Scope: the harness in `~/.claude-shared-config` (read only). Window: 2026-09-01 to 2026-11-12.

## Short answer

- The scanner [usage_scan.py](file:///Users/gamyot/Developer/grp-beklever-com/project-management/sessions/active/measuring-otter/usage_scan.py) has real blind spots. ## Task 1: detection gaps in usage_scan.py

### Method

All counts come from scripts in this folder. No transcript was loaded into a model context. The scripts honour the two library cautions:

- **Echo channel.** Tool results are never scanned. Only human prompts and tool-call inputs count. ([harness-self-management](file:///Users/gamyot/.claude/library/context/harness-self-management.md))
- **Citation is not use.** "Mentions" are reported apart from "strong signals". A strong signal is a slash command, a Skill or Agent call, a Workflow run, a prompt that starts with the item name, or a dispatch prompt that points at the definition file.

Coverage stands beside every count. Dormant is not permission to retire. ([shared-skills-harness-observatory](file:///Users/gamyot/.claude/library/context/shared-skills-harness-observatory.md))

### Why sprint-crawl cannot run today

These are the facts behind the "cannot run now" verdict. Each was checked against the files on 2026-11-13.

- `~/.claude/settings.json` has `"ralph-loop@claude-plugins-official": false`. The CLAUDE.md overnight line `/ralph-loop:ralph-loop "sprint-crawl KTP-XXX"` therefore calls a command that is not loaded.
- `~/.claude/settings.json` has `"sprint-harness@local": true`. But the local marketplace (`~/.claude/plugins/local-marketplace/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`) lists only `session`, `mapping` and `adtech`. `installed_plugins.json` has no sprint-harness entry, and there is no cache folder. The flag points at nothing.
- Also, [plugin.json](file:///Users/gamyot/.claude-shared-config/plugins/sprint-harness/plugin.json) sits at the plugin root, not in `.claude-plugin/`. The plugin would need repair before it could install.
- `/harness` is defined only in that plugin. The first step of the sprint-crawl agent (Phase 0: `/harness start`) has no command to call. The phase-gate, stop-guard, context-reinject and audit-trail hooks do not fire.
- The `sprint-crawl` agent type is still registered. Claude can dispatch it, but it breaks at Phase 0.

- **[sprint-crawl](file:///Users/gamyot/.claude-shared-config/agents/sprint-crawl.md)**, the **[sprint-harness plugin](file:///Users/gamyot/.claude-shared-config/plugins/sprint-harness/plugin.json)** and the dangling `sprint-harness@local` flag. Leave the [ralph-loop](file:///Users/gamyot/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/ralph-loop/1.0.1/commands/ralph-loop.md) plugin disabled (it is already disabled), or uninstall it.
- **[autonomous-ticket-ship](file:///Users/gamyot/.claude-shared-config/skills/autonomous-ticket-ship/SKILL.md)**. Before you archive it, check that dark-factory has its two unique ideas: safe defaults for open questions, and a morning handoff with draft MR text. - **[crawl-adversarial-review-cascade](file:///Users/gamyot/.claude-shared-config/skills/crawl-adversarial-review-cascade/SKILL.md)**. Use [adversarial-cascade](file:///Users/gamyot/.claude-shared-config/skills/adversarial-cascade/SKILL.md) for diffs and dark-factory review for ticket runs.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Pre-commit secret scan: tracked diffs + untracked files. Prints file + pattern name only, never the value.

Usage: python3 secret_scan.py <repo> [<exclude-substring> ...]
"""
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

PATTERNS = {
    "atlassian-token": r"ATATT[A-Za-z0-9_\-=]{20,}",
    "github-token": r"gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,}",
    "gitlab-token": r"glpat-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{20,}",
    "slack-token": r"xox[abprs]-[A-Za-z0-9\-]{10,}",
    "anthropic-key": r"sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{20,}",
    "openai-key": r"sk-(?!ant)[A-Za-z0-9]{32,}",
    "notion-token": r"(?:ntn|secret)_[A-Za-z0-9]{40,}",
    "google-api-key": r"AIza[0-9A-Za-z_\-]{35}",
    "aws-key": r"AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}",
    "private-key": r"-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----",
    "gcp-sa-key": r"\"private_key_id\"\s*:",
    "bearer-literal": r"Bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9\-_.]{30,}",
}
COMPILED = {k: re.compile(v) for k, v in PATTERNS.items()}

repo = Path(sys.argv[1])
excludes = sys.argv[2:]


def git(*args):
    return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), *args], capture_output=True, text=True, errors="replace").stdout


hits = []
diff = git("diff", "HEAD", "--unified=0")
current = None
for line in diff.splitlines():
    if line.startswith("+++ b/"):
        current = line[6:]
    elif line.startswith("+") and not line.startswith("+++") and current and not any(e in current for e in excludes):
        for name, rx in COMPILED.items():
            if rx.search(line):
                hits.append((current, name))
for rel in git("ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard").splitlines():
    if any(e in rel for e in excludes):
        continue
    p = repo / rel
    try:
        if p.stat().st_size > 5_000_000:
            hits.append((rel, "LARGE-FILE-skipped"))
            continue
        text = p.read_text(errors="replace")
    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
        continue
    for name, rx in COMPILED.items():
        if rx.search(text):
            hits.append((rel, name))
for f, n in sorted(set(hits)):
    print(f"HIT {n}: {f}")
print(f"scan done: {len(set(hits))} hits")

```
